transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
Lately I keep losing important things for my catering and church work—papers, lists, even ingredients—and it’s starting to mess up events I’m responsible for.

Have you had problems with losing things, staying organized, or being easily distracted since childhood, or did this start more recently? If it started recently, was it around the same time you began feeling very down or worried most days?

Actually, these issues go back to elementary school, when my teachers would complain that I was always daydreaming, losing homework, and forgetting instructions. It's been a lifelong pattern, but it became much more noticeable and disruptive about 11 months ago when I took on more unstructured work in retirement. It didn't start because I was feeling down or anxious, though the recent mistakes have definitely started to hurt my confidence.
Do these attention and organization problems happen in more than one part of your life—like at home, church, social activities, or past jobs—and have they caused real problems in those settings too?

Yes, they definitely affect multiple areas—at home my family constantly has to remind me of things, in my catering I've mixed up orders and lost recipes, and at church I've missed meetings and shown up unprepared. It's caused a lot of strain, to the point where I'm starting to turn down new projects I'd normally love because I'm afraid of letting people down.

final_diagnosis.reason: Lifelong pattern since childhood of inattention/disorganization symptoms, including losing items, forgetfulness, daydreaming, and difficulty following instructions, occurring across multiple settings and causing clear functional impairment. Symptoms worsened with increased unstructured demands but were not attributable to recent depression or anxiety based on the interview.
